episodes.title: Steady Global Economic Growth in 2027 Outlook But Risks Tilted to Downside
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
Goldman Sachs' chief economist Jan Hatzius and senior markets advisor Dominic Wilson lay out the 2027 global outlook: steady ~2.8% growth, fading fiscal/AI tailwinds, but risks skewed to the downside from energy, fiscal sustainability, and an AI investment peak. For an EM trader, the Fed's hawkish pivot and the dollar/oil trajectory are the key transmission channels.

**Key points**
- 2026 global growth ~2.7%, resilient despite Middle East war, tariffs, and higher rates; AI investment added ~0.5% to global GDP, concentrated in Taiwan/Korea.
- 2027 baseline 2.8% growth; fiscal impulse turns neutral, financial conditions boost fades, but AI capex (front-loaded) and falling oil (GS sees Brent toward $80) support income.
- US core PCE inflation elevated in low-3% range on tariff pass-through (~40bp) and energy; seen falling to 2.4% by end-2027.
- Fed hiked in September, near-certain 25bp hike in December, one more hike expected in Q1 2027 (March more likely than January); GS sees less tightening than market pricing. ECB seen hiking once in December with risk of one more in 2027; BoE one hike early 2027; outlier is BoJ, GS expects three hikes to 2% terminal, above market pricing.
- AI-driven labor market softening starting to show — frictional unemployment rise of ~0.5pp expected by 2028-30.
- French fiscal/political risk (April-May presidential election) cited as a bond-yield risk alongside US and UK fiscal paths.

**FX / rates implications**
- Dollar seen modestly softening through 2027 as energy/Fed risk premia fade, particularly against undervalued JPY (BoJ hikes, policy divergence) and CNY/CNH (large trade surplus); EUR viewed as a funding currency near-term given French election risk.
- Government bonds set up for a friendlier 2027 (higher starting yields plus gradual yield declines) versus 2026's risk-additive, yields-up/equities-down dynamic — relevant for EM rates carry trades.
- Oil risk premium has collapsed toward zero, leaving markets vulnerable to renewed Middle East escalation — a key swing factor for EM Asia importers (INR, IDR, PHP) via terms-of-trade/inflation.

**Watch list**
- December FOMC meeting: size of hike (25bp expected) and updated dot plot for 2027 guidance.
- Middle East escalation/de-escalation and its oil price impact.
- French presidential election (April-May 2027) and sovereign bond yield stress in France/euro area.
- AI capex trajectory and labor market data for signs of investment slowdown.

episodes.title: The Exchange: NVIDIA Legal Overhang, AI Sell-Off and Outage Risks
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
CNBC's The Exchange covers the rare joint DOJ/Commerce investigation into Nvidia customer Megaspeed over alleged chip-export-control violations, an AI-trade sell-off pushing much of the Nasdaq/S&P into bear-market territory, a wave of tech-sector outages, and early signs of a broader risk-off rotation (credit spreads widening, flows into Treasuries) against hawkish Fed commentary. For an EM trader the value is mainly as a read on global risk appetite and credit conditions rather than direct EM exposure.

**Key points**
- DOJ/Commerce joint statement confirms a criminal probe into Megaspeed for suspected chip-diversion/export-control violations; DOJ now leading, implying possible willful conduct carrying penalties up to 20 years; questions over what Nvidia/Jensen Wang knew.
- Wang (resigned CEO) signaled willingness to return; board reportedly won't rush succession until the independent investigation concludes; closed-door Congressional testimony next week raises the stakes.
- 61% of Nasdaq 100 and 35% of S&P 500 names are in bear-market territory; Fear & Greed index at 25/100 (extreme fear), concentrated in semis.
- Despite hawkish Fed speak, the 10-year Treasury yield slipped, suggesting bonds aren't fully buying the hawkish tone.
- Fairlead's Katie Stockton flags widening credit spreads and rotation out of equities into Treasuries as early signs of a tougher equity backdrop into next year.
- Druckenmiller reportedly short copper, a potential China-property/AI-capex-slowdown signal.
- String of outages (Salesforce -10%, Apple, NSA, Microsoft, United, banks) attributed to aging/concentrated infrastructure, not a confirmed cyberattack.
- Nvidia reports Q3 earnings after today's close; focus likely on succession/legal disclosures over guidance.

**FX / rates implications**
- A broadening equity risk-off with widening credit spreads is a classic EM carry-unwind trigger; extension would likely support USD and pressure high-beta EM Asia (KRW, TWD) and LATAM carry (BRL, MXN) tied to the AI/semis capex cycle.
- Treasury yields easing despite hawkish Fed rhetoric points to a growth-risk premium creeping in — supportive for EM local rates but a headwind for EM FX if equities keep sliding.
- A copper short flags downside risk to China/industrial demand, relevant for CLP, PEN and indirectly CNY sentiment.
- Renewed US export-control enforcement on China-bound chips is a reminder that US-China tech/trade tension remains a live tail risk for CNY/CNH and tech-exporter EM Asia FX (TWD, KRW).

**Watch list**
- Nvidia Q3 earnings tonight: guidance, succession and DOJ commentary.
- Jensen Wang's closed-door Congressional testimony next week.
- Credit-spread and Treasury/equity rotation signals flagged by Stockton as an early-2027 risk indicator.
- Progress/timeline of the DOJ-Commerce probe into Megaspeed and Nvidia export controls.

episodes.title: The Nvidious tech CEO
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
Nvidia has lost roughly $2 trillion in market value since October (stock down from ~$236 to ~$155) amid fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's resignation over a relationship tied to alleged Chinese espionage and export-control concerns. The episode frames this as a healthy, contained repricing of the AI trade rather than a systemic risk event, with implications for broader equity positioning and the bond-vs-tech rotation that matters for global risk appetite feeding into EM.

**Key points**
- Nvidia fell from ~$236 (Oct 6) to ~$155; chip index and AI-adjacent names (data-center suppliers like Caterpillar) also repriced sharply.
- S&P 500 has traded sideways since May, down from highs but not in freefall; FTSE 100 has outperformed the S&P 500 YTD as a "boring," non-tech haven.
- Bank of America fund manager survey: largest pullout of tech allocation since 2006, alongside a meaningful rotation into bonds (investors remain underweight bonds but are closing the gap).
- 5-year UST yields ~4.96%, framed as attractive real yield (~2% after assumed 3% inflation) with limited duration risk versus the 10-year.
- Anthropic's IPO prices this week (trades Thursday) — seen as a major confidence test for AI/tech market appetite; a bad debut could trigger broader "I'm out of tech" sentiment.

**FX / rates implications**
- This is a global risk-sentiment story, not an EM-specific one: an orderly AI-sector derating (vs. a disorderly, contagious one) supports continued risk-on carry positioning in EM FX/rates; a disorderly outcome (e.g., a botched Anthropic IPO) would be the trigger to watch for broad risk-off that pressures EM Asia and LatAm currencies via USD safe-haven flows and UST demand.
- Rotation into bonds (5y UST yields near 5%) modestly supports the front-end-anchored carry backdrop EM rates traders price off of; no direct Fed/dollar-policy view is discussed.

**Watch list**
- Nvidia's first post-Jensen earnings release (same day as this episode) for guidance/governance signals.
- Anthropic IPO: prices Wednesday, trades Thursday — outcome will be read as a referendum on AI-sector risk appetite.
- Further Bank of America fund manager survey data on tech vs. bond allocation shifts.
